clips.text_zh: 又係咁。BTC 橫盤兩三個禮拜冇人理，pump 完 15% 突然個個衝入去。我都係廢柴一個，止損又遲。考牌都未溫完，又輸一注。ok 當交學費。🙏
clips.text_en_b1: Why does everyone buy BTC after the pump? You watch BTC do nothing for weeks, ignore it completely. Then it pumps 15% and suddenly everyone wants in. This pattern repeats again and again. Buying after the move already happened is just paying tuition to the market.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread on chasing BTC after it already moved

signal.rationale: Post is observational complaint about retail chasing, no setup

clips.text_en_b2: Why does the crowd always pile into BTC once the pump has already happened? You can watch it sit flat for weeks on end with absolutely no interest, and then the moment it surges 15% out of nowhere, every retail trader suddenly wants a piece of the action. This keeps repeating itself over and over, and chasing the move after it has played out is essentially paying tuition fees to the market. Once again, I got stopped out far too late.
clips.text_en_c1: It is the same maddening cycle that plays out every single time. Bitcoin idles sideways for two or three weeks, attracting precisely zero attention from retail traders, and then the moment it pumps fifteen percent, the FOMO crowd piles in en masse. Chasing an asset after the move has already occurred is, in effect, handing the market a tuition fee in exchange for nothing more than a bruised ego and a lighter portfolio. If you had bought during the boredom phase, you would have been positioned long before the herd arrived, but watching paint dry requires a discipline that most participants simply do not possess.
clips.text_en_c2: There is a pattern so consistent it borders on ritual. Bitcoin consolidates sideways for two or three weeks, drawing precisely zero retail interest, until a fifteen-percent vertical move materialises overnight, at which point every laggard and their mother scrambles to pile in at the top. Capital preserved is capital earned, yet here I am, stop-loss once again triggered late, watching another position bleed out while my licensing exam revision sits untouched on the desk. The market, ever the patient pedagogue, has extracted another installment of tuition. Consider the lesson learned; consider, also, the asymmetric cost of ignoring it.

clips.text_zh: 留意 SpaceX IPO。2026 年 9 月 9 號大約 3.19 億股解禁，大概係 baseline pool 7%、總股本 2.4%。IPO 後第 90 個交易日，第三次大解禁。Tesla 都係咁玩法，散戶接晒貨。🧐
clips.text_en_b1: On September 9, 2026, around 319 million extra SpaceX shares become eligible to sell. That is about 7% of the baseline pool and roughly 2.4% of total shares outstanding. It marks 90 trading days since the IPO and the third major lockup release event. Big supply dump incoming.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread on SpaceX IPO lockup release schedule

signal.rationale: Watch Sept 9 SpaceX unlock as overhang risk for Musk-linked names

clips.text_en_b2: Anyone keeping an eye on the SpaceX IPO situation should know that around 319 million shares are set to unlock on September 9, 2026, which translates to roughly 7% of the baseline pool and approximately 2.4% of total shares outstanding. This marks the third major lockup release, falling exactly 90 trading days after the listing. The pattern mirrors what happened with that company, where retail investors ended up absorbing the bulk of the supply being dumped onto the market.
clips.text_en_c1: Mark your calendars for the ninth of September, 2026, because approximately 319 million additional SpaceX shares will become eligible for sale at that point. That figure corresponds to roughly seven percent of the baseline insider pool and around two-point-four percent of total shares outstanding, marking the third major lockup expiry since the company's IPO and falling on the ninetieth trading day post-listing. Historically, such events have triggered significant supply pressure, with retail bagholders being the ones left holding depreciated positions, exactly as happened repeatedly with Tesla. Unless institutional buyers step in to absorb the overhang, one should brace for a meaningful correction.
clips.text_en_c2: Investors with exposure to SpaceX ought to mark September 9, 2026, in their calendars with appropriate foreboding. Approximately 319 million shares become eligible for resale that day, constituting some seven percent of the baseline pool and roughly two-point-four percent of total shares outstanding. This represents the third major lockup expiry event since the IPO, falling precisely on the ninetieth trading day post-listing. History, as Tesla holders will attest with weary familiarity, rhymes rather than repeats: institutional insiders distribute, retail absorbs the overhang, and price discovery suffers accordingly. A non-trivial supply shock is therefore imminent, and the prudent position is to recognise it.

clips.text_zh: 而家啲人成日叫人買 ChatGPT / Claude 最貴個 tier。wtf，Qwen 同 GLM 平九成都夠我用。我考牌溫書都靠 AI 續命，唔使俾咁多 subscription。👍
clips.text_en_b1: Have you noticed this type of post? People keep telling you to try the PAID model tier, saying ChatGPT or Claude is so scary you have to pay for it. Why does nobody mention cheaper models like Kimi, GLM or Qwen? Those give you easily 90% of the performance for maybe 10% of the price.
clips.source_hint: /g/ thread complaining about shilling for paid AI tiers
clips.text_en_b2: Have you noticed how every other thread these days is pushing you towards the priciest subscription tier of ChatGPT or Claude, as though those models are the only ones worth bothering with? Meanwhile, alternatives such as Kimi, Qwen and GLM deliver roughly 90% of the performance at perhaps 10% of the cost, yet hardly anyone seems to mention them. Personally, I've been getting through my licensing exam revision with AI doing the heavy lifting, and I can't justify splashing out on expensive monthly subscriptions when…
clips.text_en_c1: It is genuinely bewildering how aggressively people push the premium tiers of ChatGPT and Claude, framing them as indispensable tools that any serious user simply must subscribe to. Meanwhile, models such as Qwen, GLM and Kimi deliver what is arguably ninety percent of the performance at a mere fraction of the cost, often less than ten percent of what the flagship subscriptions charge on a monthly basis. Whether you are cramming for professional licensing exams or simply conducting research, these open-weight alternatives are more than sufficient for the vast majority of practical workloads.
clips.text_en_c2: One observes, with mounting exasperation, that the discourse surrounding ChatGPT and Claude has calcified into quasi-religious evangelism for the priciest subscription tier. Yet the open-source alternatives, Kimi, GLM, and Qwen chief among them, deliver what any rational assessment must concede is ninety percent of the capability at a tenth of the cost. I have, for the record, been sustaining my professional licensing studies almost entirely on these leaner models, and the marginal performance differential is, for my purposes, indistinguishable from noise. The subscription industrial complex, it seems, thrives on manufactured inadequacy more than on any genuine technical merit.

clips.text_zh: pol 板啲人成日問 Musk 權力有幾高。btw 美國 21 間銀行合搞 stablecoin，Apple Coin、Tesla Coin、X Coin 排住隊出。HK 樓咁細、租金咁貴，呢邊真係搵唔到未來。lol
clips.text_en_b1: How high do you think Elon Musk's true power level is? Twenty-one U.S. banks are already planning to launch a joint stablecoin. Soon you will see Apple Coin, Google Coin, Microsoft Coin, Tesla Coin, X Coin and Bank Coin flooding the market. One anon asked this on /pol/ tonight.
clips.source_hint: /pol/ thread asking about Musk's real political power
clips.text_en_b2: How much genuine influence do you reckon Elon Musk actually wields at this point? Twenty-one American banks are already collaborating on a joint stablecoin venture, and once that framework lands you can bet your bottom dollar the floodgates will open. Expect Apple Coin, Google Coin, Microsoft Coin, Tesla Coin, X Coin and Bank Coin to come pouring out one after another.
clips.text_en_c1: A perennial debate on /pol/ concerns the true extent of Elon Musk's political and financial influence, and recent developments suggest that the answer is, quite frankly, far greater than most casual observers assume. Twenty-one American banks have already formalised plans to launch a joint stablecoin, which would fundamentally reshape the digital payments landscape once it reaches the market. Beyond that, Apple Coin, Google Coin, Microsoft Coin, Tesla Coin, X Coin and the inevitable Bank Coin are all reportedly queued for release in rapid succession. For those trapped in jurisdictions where housing is absurdly small and rents remain punishingly high, the technological momentum happening elsewhere is, to put it mildly, demoralising.
clips.text_en_c2: An inquiry surfaced tonight regarding the true apex of Elon Musk's influence, and the timing proves instructive. Twenty-one American banks, acting in concert, are poised to unveil a joint stablecoin, while Apple, Google, Microsoft, Tesla, and X queue with their own branded variants in what can only be described as a coordinated assault on monetary sovereignty itself. The consolidation of technological and financial power under a handful of unaccountable actors proceeds with such velocity that one is left to wonder whether the regulatory apparatus retains any meaningful purchase. From a city whose housing stock has shrunk beneath its populace and whose rents have soared beyond reason, the future looks decidedly elsewhere.

clips.text_zh: lol Blue Archive 班開發者出新 3D game Fareidolia。一個時代結束。S15 我都未睇完，又多樣嘢要追。溫完 HKIE 先講。🙏
clips.text_en_b1: Blue Archive developers are now turning their attention elsewhere with a new game called Fareidolia. The new 3D anime game project, previously known as RX, was officially announced alongside new story details. Fans are calling this the end of an era for the franchise.
clips.source_hint: /v/ thread on Blue Archive devs announcing Fareidolia
clips.text_en_b2: It looks like the Blue Archive development team have finally moved on, having officially unveiled a brand-new 3D anime game called Fareidolia, the very project that had previously circulated under the codename RX. Alongside the announcement, fresh story details were also shared, and longtime fans are already mourning the moment as the end of an era for the franchise. Meanwhile, I'm still struggling to finish watching Season 15, and now there's yet another title added to my ever-growing backlog.
clips.text_en_c1: The developers behind Blue Archive have officially unveiled Fareidolia, a brand-new three-dimensional anime project that was previously circulating under the codename RX. The announcement, which dropped alongside preliminary story details and character concepts, has been received by longtime fans as a symbolic passing of the torch, if not the outright end of an era for the franchise they once championed. Given that Season Fifteen has not yet been fully watched and professional licensing exam preparation looms, this represents yet another item on an already overflowing queue of media to consume. One can only hope that the quality matches the nostalgia.
clips.text_en_c2: Blue Archive, that venerable cornerstone of one's anime gaming routine, appears to be entering its twilight chapter as the development studio pivots attention toward Fareidolia, a freshly unveiled three-dimensional project previously circulating under the codename RX. New story details accompanied the announcement, and the prevailing sentiment across fan communities suggests an epoch has effectively concluded. Season fifteen of the existing title remains, for this correspondent, stubbornly unfinished, and now yet another entry joins the queue. Professional licensing examinations will, regrettably, take precedence; the Fareidolia rabbit hole must perforce wait its turn. One mourns, briefly, the inexorable passage of eras.

clips.text_zh: 我同 fit 板個 post 一樣樣。日日行 15k-20k steps，食又 cut 500 卡，total 1000 kcal deficit。4 個禮拜個 scale 唔郁。但條命照返，肥仔信今日又 tag 我去 gym。靠 AI 續命。
clips.text_en_b1: Can't burn fat. I'm at 18% body fat. I walk 15k to 20k steps a day, burning 500 to 800 calories just from walking. Plus a 500 calorie food cut, so a 1000 kcal daily deficit. Progressive overload still works and my muscles are getting bigger. But the scale isn't moving after 4 weeks. 90k steps a week on average.
clips.source_hint: /fit/ thread on stalled cut despite big deficit
clips.text_en_b2: I'm stuck in exactly the same situation as the guy who posted on /fit/. I'm sitting at around 18% body fat and clocking in anywhere between 15,000 and 20,000 steps a day, which on its own burns through 500 to 800 calories. On top of that, I've trimmed roughly 500 calories from my diet, putting me at a solid 1000 kcal daily deficit, and progressive overload is still doing its job because my muscles are visibly growing.
clips.text_en_c1: Despite maintaining a daily regimen of fifteen to twenty thousand steps, sustaining a five-hundred-calorie dietary cut and operating at a total deficit of roughly one thousand kilocalories, the scale remains stubbornly stationary after four consecutive weeks. Progressive overload in the gym continues to function as intended, and muscle growth is visibly occurring, which would normally suggest that body recomposition is taking place beneath the surface. Yet the numbers on the weighing machine refuse to cooperate, hovering around eighteen percent body fat without any meaningful downward movement, even though weekly step totals consistently exceed ninety thousand.
clips.text_en_c2: Plateaus, the inveterate torment of every dedicated lifter, have apparently come for me with characteristic indifference. I presently sit at roughly eighteen percent body fat, clocking between fifteen and twenty thousand daily steps, which yields some five-to-eight hundred kilocalories of expenditure before any structured exercise. A further five-hundred-calorie dietary reduction produces a daily deficit comfortably north of one thousand kilocalories. Progressive overload continues to function as advertised, muscle accrues incrementally, yet after four weeks the scale has registered precisely nothing. Ninety thousand weekly steps, sustained religiously, and the number refuses to budge. Adaptive thermogenesis, water retention, or some other metabolic sleight of hand is presumably to blame.

clips.text_zh: /a/ 板有人問動漫女角巨乳幾大先算過火。lol Gundam 00 同 Demon Slayer 起碼有個比例。考牌溫到眼花，上嚟笑下都好。🧐
clips.text_en_b1: When it comes to anime and manga busts, how big is too big? One anon asked this on /a/ tonight and the thread is full of clips from old series and sketches. Some replies joke that physics stopped applying decades ago. Others say the limit is when the character cannot stand up straight anymore.
clips.source_hint: /a/ thread on absurd anime bust sizes
clips.text_en_b2: When it comes to character designs in anime and manga, where exactly do you draw the line on bust size before things cross into ridiculous territory? An anon posed that very question on /a/ tonight, and predictably the thread has exploded into a chaotic collage of classic series clips, rough sketches and heated debate. Some commenters joke that realism stopped being a consideration decades ago, while others insist the breaking point arrives the moment the poor character can no longer stand up straight without toppling…
clips.text_en_c1: An anonymous poster on /a/ recently posed the eternal question of where exactly the line should be drawn when it comes to anatomical proportions in anime and manga, particularly with regard to bust size. The thread promptly descended into chaos, accumulating clips from older series alongside hastily sketched comparisons, with contributors debating whether shows such as Gundam 00 and Demon Slayer at least respected basic ratios. Some respondents argued that physics ceased to apply several decades ago, while others insisted that the threshold is reached the moment a character can no longer stand upright without compromising her centre of gravity. It is, at its core, an unanswerable question.
clips.text_en_c2: A thread on /a/ tonight posed a question as old as fan service itself: at what magnitude do illustrated endowments cross the threshold from anatomical suggestion into outright thermodynamic impossibility? The replies, predictably, form a curated museum of absurdities, screenshot evidence culled from decades of increasingly unmoored character design. Certain contributors observe, with no small weariness, that physics ceased to apply to the genre somewhere around the late nineties; others, more pragmatically, identify the precise breaking point as the moment a figure can no longer maintain an upright posture. One continues revising for professional examinations until one's eyes blur, and such diversions provide, at minimum, palliative amusement.
